profile.campus_mw_context: The 128,715-sq. ft. data center in Sterling, VA, offers 11 MW of IT capacity and features robust connectivity options with high bandwidth and high-availability circuits and a number of metro and long-haul networks.

reading.body:
CyrusOne NVA4 in Sterling, Virginia publishes 11 MW of IT capacity across 128,715 square feet, a mid-sized facility that ranks 26th among Virginia data centers with disclosed capacity.

The pattern here is disclosure, not size. Virginia has 330 mapped data centers, but only 25 publish capacity figures, totaling 1,603 MW. NVA4 is one of the 25, and its 11 MW is less than 1% of that disclosed total. The 305 facilities without published capacity are the larger unknown, and they sit in the same state as this one.

For AI specifically, 11 MW bounds what this building can do. At a common AI training density of 40 kW per rack, that is roughly 275 racks of compute, which is not a frontier training footprint. The facility's emphasis on metro and long-haul network circuits points to distributed training and inference, where data movement matters more than raw power density. Power, not networking, is the constraint that keeps a site like this out of the top tier.

What the data does not say is how much capacity Virginia actually holds. The 1,603 MW figure covers only the 25 facilities that disclose, and the remaining 305 could include campuses far larger than this one. NVA4's rank of 26th is a rank among the disclosed, not among the built.
